channel.description: A daily brief. Each story is one event told through outlets that disagree — differences named in plain words, every source linked, coverage gaps measured. Then it ends.

item.title: eto — Monday, September 28, 2026
item.description: The Monday, September 28, 2026 edition: 3 stories, each one event told through outlets that disagree.
item.content:encoded:
Markets

  • S&P 500 7743.41
  • S&P/TSX 35800.89
  • USD/CAD 1.4145
  • Bank of Canada overnight rate 2.25

Business news

  • 10-year U.S. Treasury yield reaches highest level since 2007 — MarketWatch
  • PB Fintech’s $3.3 Billion Rout Fuels Rush Into Leveraged Bets — Bloomberg · Traders piled into leveraged bets on Temasek-backed PB Fintech Ltd. as the stock lost $3.3 billion in market value on Thursday after India’s insurance regulator proposed caps on commissions and management expenses.
  • Director/PDMR Shareholding — Financial Post · Wael Sawan, Sinead Gorman, Philippa Bounds, Peter Costello, Cederic Cremers, Machteld de Haan, Andrew Smith, Rachel Solway each acquired dividend shares in Shell plc. Transactions occurred in Amsterdam, London, New York on 24 September 2026.
  • London’s Bridge TroublesSpread with Waterlooat Risk of Closure — Bloomberg · London's Waterloo Bridge faces closure within three years without urgent repairs, deepening concerns over the UK capital's crumbling river crossings. Are London's bridges really falling down? Harry Black explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
  • International Petroleum Corporation Announces Results of Normal Course Issuer Bid — Financial Post · International Petroleum Corporation repurchased 148,500 common shares under its NCIB from September 21 to 25, 2026, totaling 1,099,086 shares as of September 25, 2026.
  • Yangarra Announces Operations Update — Financial Post · Yangarra drills 17 Belly River wells, spends $58 million, expects $45 million cash flow by end of Q3 2026, with 1,450 boe/d production and 106 future drilling locations.
  • Yen Gains After Japan’s Currency Czar Warns Against Weakness — Bloomberg · The yen surged, erasing earlier losses, after Japan’s currency czar issued another warning about its weakness.
  • Extended hours for stock trading comes to Canada — The Globe and Mail · CIX Trading launching platform that will allow trading from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET, with plans to extend window later this year
  • Remote work is finally ending as the pandemic era fades — The Globe and Mail · Employers want more of the spontaneous collaborative interaction that can only happen in the workplace
  • To resist American domination, Canada must fix its failing tax system — The Globe and Mail · As competition heats up, the country needs to use all the tools it can to develop an attractive environment for investment and growth

Writers

  • AI and the Fall? of the Creative Class — Apricitas Economics · America is Losing Hundreds of Thousands of Jobs in Media, Film & the Arts. How Much is AI to Blame?

The brief ends here.
